newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends mixed, focus on July/Sept spread.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends mixed, focus on July/Sept spread.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended narrowly mixed on Tuesday, as traders focused on rolling over and liquidating the July contract ahead of its first notice day July 17, dealers said.
"People are getting out of harm's way ahead of first notice day," one trader said. "Basically there was trade and spec long liquidation and a lot of July/Septs traded."
July cocoa closed at $1,449 a tonne, unchanged on the day, after ranging from $1,458 to $1,441. Second-month September rose $3, to $1,488, while the back months sagged $1.

Cocoa prices weakened at the outset, as speculators followed through on the market's two-day sell-off, traders said. Downward momentum picked up after the July contract breached key support at $1,444, triggering light commission house sell-stops.
But scale-down industry held off further losses and prompted the ring to cover their short positions. Long liquidation and rollovers, however, pushed prices back towards unchanged.

With July open interest at 26,820 lots as of June 2 and only two weeks to go until the spot contract enters delivery period, traders expect the market to remain under pressure as speculators continue to liquidate or rollover Julys.
"It's only just begun with the July structure," said a trader, "and the specs have more to go."
The July/September switch ended at $39 compared to $36 at the close on Monday, and some traders expect the contango to widen further.
Technically, traders pegged July support near $1,440-$1,439. Near-term resistance was seen at $1,465-$1,467.
